item_name: Apple iMac 21.5" Retina 4K Late 2015 Logic Board (A1418 / EMC 2833)

data.donor_machine: iMac 21.5" Retina 4K, Late 2015 — A1418, EMC 2833, iMac16,2
data.cpu: Intel Core i5 3.1 GHz quad-core (i5-5675R, Broadwell) with Iris Pro 6200 graphics
data.cpu_source: Read directly off the CPU label on the board — stamped 3.1G. Not inferred. everymac narrowed the serial to i5 3.1 or i7 3.3; the label settled it.
data.ram: 8 GB LPDDR3, four soldered Samsung modules. Confirmed by Geoff visually. Not slotted, not upgradeable — the board carries CPU and RAM as one fixed unit.
data.ram_part: Samsung K4E6E304EE-EGCF, date code 546 (week 46 of 2015, mid-November) — consistent with a Late 2015 build, so the memory is original to the machine.
data.working_status: Donor machine was in perfect working condition when the display cracked. Board pulled from a fully functional machine, not a dead one.
data.why_parted_out: Screen physically cracked; Geoff pulled the drive and disassembled the rest.
data.batch_note: One of three listings split from a single parted-out iMac. Siblings: imac-2015-4k-power-board, imac-2015-4k-cooling-parts. Rear shell deliberately retired to Geoff's DIY pile, not listed — too bulky and low-value to ship under baked-in free shipping.
data.title_hints: Lead with A1418 / EMC 2833 / i5 3.1GHz / 8GB. Repair buyers search the model and EMC, and the Iris Pro 6200 is the better iGPU of that generation and worth naming.

selling_points: Pulled from a fully working machine, display cracked — not an untested or dead-machine board
Iris Pro 6200, the better integrated GPU of that generation
Board serial C02551300WSGQRXAA is listable so a buyer can verify
RAM date code matches the build, so the board is original to the machine
data.ram_density_check: Samsung K4E6E304xx is a 16 Gb package = 2 GB per chip. Four chips = 8 GB, which independently confirms Geoff's recollection and rules out 16 GB (that would need 32 Gb chips). 8 GB was the standard build on the 4K 21.5" Late 2015 with 16 GB as the BTO.
data.shipping: Small and light, ships cheap in a padded box with antistatic wrap. Free shipping baked into price per house style costs little here, unlike the shell.

data.rationale: Deliberately short. eBay AND-matches every word in the title, so long queries return almost nothing — the MacBook run proved this. The broad first term pulls 2012-2017 A1418 boards for pool depth and gets filtered by year from the titles; the EMC term is the sharp one since parts sellers list it.
data.how_to_run: SerpAPI cannot fetch sold listings any more (see GOTCHAS, eBay login wall). Run each on eBay logged in, filter to Sold, sort by Ended Recently, then Cmd+A / Cmd+C the page into comps.txt. All three into one file is fine.
data.expectation: Expect a thin pool. Parts boards move slowly. Under 5 usable comps triggers the skill's thin-pool protocol and conservative pricing.
